He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Duquesne Dukes men's basketball|Duquesne Dukes]] and the [[Arizona Wildcats men's basketball|Arizona Wildcats]]. After going undrafted, McConnell joined the [[Philadelphia 76ers]] in 2015 and spent four seasons with the team before signing with the Pacers in 2019. ==High school career== McConnell attended [[Chartiers Valley High School]] in the [[Pittsburgh]]-area borough of [[Bridgeville, Pennsylvania]], where he played for his father, Tim. As team captain his senior year, he averaged 34.2 points, 8.2 rebounds and 9.1 assists per game,{{cite news |date=March 20, 2015 |title=15 things you probably don't know about T.J. McConnell |url=https://tucson.com/sports/college/wildcats/things-you-probably-don-t-know-about-t-j-mcconnell/collection_73426dae-cf46-11e4-816d-3bc4d2b3adec.html |access-date=October 26, 2015 |work=Arizona Daily Star}} earned first-team all-state honors, and was named the [[Associated Press]]'s Pennsylvania Class 3A Player of the Year male athlete of the year for all sports by the [[Pittsburgh Post-Gazette]]. He led the Colts to a 29–2 record, the [[Western Pennsylvania Interscholastic Athletic League|WPIAL]] championship, and a berth in the Class 3A state championship game as a senior, which they lost to Philadelphia's [[Saints John Neumann and Maria Goretti Catholic High School|Neumann-Goretti]].{{cite web | url=https://www.arizonawildcats.com/ViewArticle.dbml?DB_OEM_ID=30700&ATCLID=207988081 | title=T.J. McConnell Biography | work=ArizonaWildcats.com | access-date=March 29, 2014}}{{cite web|url=https://www.pennlive.com/highschoolsports/article/neumann-goretti-hangs-on-to-beat-chartiers-valley-65-63-in-piaa-class-aaa-basketball-championship/|title=Neumann-Goretti hangs on to beat Chartiers Valley 65-63 in PIAA Class AAA basketball championship|author=Michael Bullock|access-date=October 22, 2024|date=March 27, 2010}} ==College career== [[File:T. J. McConnell looking up.jpg|thumb|left|T.J. McConnell for Arizona in 2014]] As a freshman for [[Duquesne Dukes men's basketball|Duquesne]] in 2010–11, McConnell averaged 10.8 points, 3.8 rebounds, 4.4 assists, and 2.8 steals per game in 32 appearances (30 starts), earning 2011 Atlantic 10 Freshman of the Year honors. As a sophomore in 2011–12, he averaged 11.4 points, 4.4 rebounds, 5.5 assists, and 2.8 steals per game, helping the Dukes to a 16–15 record and earning third-team All-Atlantic 10 Conference honors and a spot on the A-10 All-Defensive Team. In April 2012, he transferred to [[Arizona Wildcats men's basketball|Arizona]] where he was subsequently forced to sit out the 2012–13 season due to NCAA transfer rules.{{cite web|url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/1139829-arizona-basketball-former-duquesne-pg-tj-mcconnell-transfers-to-arizona|title=Arizona Basketball: Former Duquesne PG T.J. McConnell Transfers to Arizona|work=Bleacher Report|date=April 10, 2012|access-date=September 27, 2015}} McConnell's transfer was motivated by a desire to compete for a [[National championships in men's college basketball|national championship]].{{cite news|last1=Kilgore|first1=Adam|title=T.J. McConnell's journey from NCAA tournament spectator to Duquesne transfer to Arizona's engine|url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/news/sports/wp/2015/03/25/how-t-j-mcconnell-went-from-ncaa-tournament-spectator-to-duquesne-transfer-to-arizonas-engine/|access-date=January 30, 2017|newspaper=Washington Post|date=March 25, 2015}} In the 2013–14 season, McConnell helped lead the Wildcats to a 21–0 record to start the season before teammate [[Brandon Ashley]] injured his foot and was sidelined for the rest of the season. The season culminated in an [[Elite Eight|Elite 8]] appearance for the Wildcats.{{cite web|last1=Amacher|first1=Ezra|title=2013-14 Season in Review|url=https://pointguardu.com/2013-14-season-in-review/|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141129081507/http://pointguardu.com/2013-14-season-in-review/|url-status=dead|archive-date=November 29, 2014|website=PointguardU.com|publisher=Gopher Media|date=March 31, 2014|access-date=November 24, 2014}} As a senior, McConnell was voted first-team [[List of All-Pac-12 Conference men's basketball teams|All-Pac-12]] and named to the Pac-12 All-Defensive Team, and he helped lead Arizona to another appearance in the Elite Eight, where they lost to the Wisconsin Badgers for a second consecutive season.{{cite press release|title=2014-15 Pac-12 Conference Men's Basketball Honors|date=March 9, 2015|publisher=Pac-12|url=https://pac-12.com/news/2015/3/9/2014-15-pac-12-conference-mens-basketball-honors.aspx|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150312012307/http://pac-12.com/article/2015/03/09/2014-15-pac-12-conference-mens-basketball-honors|archive-date=March 12, 2015|url-status=live}} On December 18, 2024 McConnell became the 34th Arizona Wildcat to have his name inducted into the [[Arizona Wildcats men's basketball#Arizona's Ring of Honor|Arizona Basketball Ring of Honor]], doing so by playing 10 years in the NBA.{{cite web |title=T.J. McConnell To Be Inducted Into Arizona Ring of Honor on Dec. 18 |url=https://arizonawildcats.com/news/2024/12/5/mens-basketball-t-j-mcconnell-to-be-inducted-into-arizona-ring-of-honor-on-dec-18.aspx}} ==Professional career== [[File:T.J. McConnell pregame with the Philadelphia 76ers in 2015.JPG|thumb|right|McConnell during pregame warmups]] ===Philadelphia 76ers (2015–2019)=== After going undrafted in the [[2015 NBA draft]], McConnell joined his home state team the [[Philadelphia 76ers]] for the [[2015 NBA Summer League]].{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/sixers/news/150711-vegas-info|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190406005800/https://www.nba.com/sixers/news/150711-vegas-info|archive-date=April 6, 2019|title=Las Vegas Summer League Roster & Schedule|work=NBA.com|date=July 11, 2015|access-date=October 22, 2024}} On September 27, 2015, he signed with the 76ers.{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/sixers/news/sixers-announce-2015-training-camp-roster|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191202212412/https://www.nba.com/sixers/news/sixers-announce-2015-training-camp-roster|archive-date=December 2, 2019|title=SIXERS ANNOUNCE 2015 TRAINING CAMP ROSTER|work=NBA.com|date=September 27, 2015|access-date=October 22, 2024}} He played well during preseason, averaging 6.2 points and 4.8 assists in five games, earning himself a spot on the 76ers' opening night roster.{{cite web|last=White|first=Mike|url=https://www.post-gazette.com/sports/high-school-basketball/2015/10/26/Chartiers-Valley-High-School-grad-T-J-McConnell-makes-NBA-team-Philadelphia-76ers/stories/201510260194|title=Chartiers Valley High School grad T.J. McConnell makes NBA team|work=Post-Gazette.com|date=October 26, 2015|access-date=October 26, 2015}} McConnell went on to make his NBA debut in the team's season opener against the [[2015–16 Boston Celtics season|Boston Celtics]] on October 28. In 27 minutes of action, he recorded four points, four assists, and three steals in a 112–95 loss.{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/game/phi-vs-bos-0021500005/box-score|title=phi vs bos|work=NBA.com|date=October 28, 2015|access-date=October 22, 2024}} On February 6, 2016, while starting at point guard in place of the injured [[Ish Smith]], McConnell tied his season-high of 17 points in a 103–98 win over the [[2015–16 Brooklyn Nets season|Brooklyn Nets]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story?id=14729723&src=desktop|title=Okafor, Noel lead 76ers past Nets|work=NBA.com|date=February 6, 2016|access-date=October 22, 2024}} On March 23, in a loss to the [[2015—16 Denver Nuggets season|Denver Nuggets]], he had a 17-point outing for a third time in 2015–16.{{cite web|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/m/mccontj01/gamelog/2016/|title=T.J. McConnell 2015-16 Game Log|work=Basketball-Reference.com|access-date=December 11, 2016}} At the season's end, he received two votes in the 2016 [[NBA All-Rookie Team]] voting.{{cite web|url=https://pr.nba.com/2015-16-nba-all-rookie-team/|title=2015-16 NBA All-Rookie teams|work=NBA.com|date=May 19, 2016|access-date=October 22, 2024}} [[File:T.J. McConnell, Bradley Beal (cropped).jpg|thumb|left|McConnell defending against [[Washington Wizards]]' [[Bradley Beal]] in February 2018]] In July 2016, McConnell rejoined the 76ers for the [[2016 NBA Summer League]].{{cite web|first=Ray|last=Boyd|url=https://philadelphia.cbslocal.com/2016/07/01/ben-simmons-headlines-sixers-summer-league-roster/|title=Ben Simmons Headlines Sixers Summer League Roster|work=CBSLocal.com|date=July 1, 2016|access-date=January 4, 2017}} On December 11, 2016, he had a near triple-double with 12 points, 10 rebounds and nine assists in a 97–79 win over the [[2016–17 Detroit Pistons season|Detroit Pistons]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400899798|title=Covington scores 16 for 76ers in 97-79 win over Pistons|work=ESPN.com|date=December 11, 2016|access-date=December 11, 2016}} On January 6, 2017, he had a career-high 17 assists in a 110–106 loss to the [[2016–17 Boston Celtics season|Boston Celtics]], becoming just the fourth player in franchise history to hit that mark in a single contest. His total was two off the Philadelphia's all-time record of 19 assists, initially set by [[Maurice Cheeks]] in 1987, and later matched by [[Dana Barros]] in 1995.{{cite web|last=Seltzer|first=Brian|url=https://www.nba.com/sixers/news/buzzer|title=Game Recap: Celtics Outlast Sixers, 110-106|work=NBA.com|date=January 6, 2017|access-date=January 7, 2017}} McConnell hit a game-winning buzzer beater against the [[2016–17 New York Knicks season|New York Knicks]] with a turnaround jump shot on the baseline on January 11.{{cite web|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-pacdLuoWDE|title=T.J. McConnell Turnaround Jumper to Beat Knicks | Tissot Buzzer Beater | 01.11.17|work=YouTube.com|publisher=NBA|date=January 11, 2017|access-date=September 4, 2017}} On November 25, 2017, McConnell had 15 points and 13 assists in a 130–111 win over the [[2017–18 Orlando Magic season|Orlando Magic]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400975029|title=J.J. Redick hits 8 3s, 76ers send Magic to 8th straight loss|work=ESPN.com|date=November 25, 2017|access-date=November 25, 2017}} On January 15, 2018, he scored a career-high 18 points in a 117–111 win over the [[2017–18 Toronto Raptors season|Toronto Raptors]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400975385|title=Joel Embiid, 76ers barely hold on, edge Raptors 117-111|work=ESPN.com|date=January 15, 2018|access-date=January 15, 2018}} On February 12, McConnell recorded his first career triple-double with 10 points, 10 rebounds and 11 assists in a 108–92 win over the [[2017–18 New York Knicks season|New York Knicks]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400975588|title=Saric scores 24 to lead 76ers past slumping Knicks|work=ESPN.com|date=February 12, 2018|access-date=February 12, 2018}} He also matched a career high with six steals and became the first player in franchise history to record a triple-double off the bench.{{cite web|last=Seltzer|first=Brian|url=http://www.nba.com/sixers/news/buzzer-mcconnell-triple-double-helps-spur-win-over-knicks|title=Game Recap | McConnell Triple-Double Helps Spur Win Over Knicks|work=NBA.com|date=February 12, 2018|access-date=February 12, 2018}}{{cite web|last=Spears|first=Justin|url=http://tucson.com/sports/arizonawildcats/basketball/t-j-mcconnell-records-first-career-triple-double-in-the/article_573bde42-1066-11e8-b239-a784174fee5d.html|title=T.J. McConnell records first career triple-double in the 76ers' win over the Knicks|work=tucson.com|date=February 12, 2018|access-date=February 12, 2018}} In Game 4 of the 76ers' second-round playoff series against the [[2017–18 Boston Celtics season|Boston Celtics]], McConnell had a career-high 19 points, seven rebounds, and five assists in a 103–92 win, helping Philadelphia cut the series deficit to 3–1.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401031674|title=McConnell helps 76ers hold off elimination against Boston|work=ESPN.com|date=May 7, 2018|access-date=May 7, 2018}} On June 13, the 76ers announced they had exercised the fourth-year option on their contract with McConnell.{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/sixers/philadelphia-76ers-exercise-contract-options-tj-mcconnell-and-richaun-holmes|title=Philadelphia 76ers Exercise Contract Options for T.J. McConnell and Richaun Holmes|work=NBA.com|date=June 13, 2018|access-date=June 13, 2018}} McConnell made 76 appearances (including three starts) in his [[2018–19 NBA season|final season]] for the 76ers, recording averages of 6.4 points, 2.3 rebounds, and 3.4 assists.{{Cite web|title=T.J. McConnell 2018-19 Stats per Game|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/player/gamelog/_/id/2530530/type/nba/year/2019|access-date=May 4, 2026|website=espn.com|language=en}} ===Indiana Pacers (2019–present)=== On July 3, 2019, McConnell signed a two-year contract worth $7 million with the [[Indiana Pacers]].{{Cite web|url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/2690122-report-former-76ers-pg-tj-mcconnell-signs-2-year-7m-contract-with-pacers|title = Report: Former 76ers PG T.J. McConnell Signs 2-Year, $7M Contract with Pacers|website = [[Bleacher Report]]}} He compiled 71 appearances (including three starts) for the Pacers during the [[2019–20 NBA season]], recording averages of 6.5 points, 2.7 rebounds, and 5.0 assists.{{Cite web|title=T.J. McConnell 2019-20 Stats per Game|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/player/gamelog/_/id/2530530/type/nba/year/2020|access-date=May 4, 2026|website=espn.com|language=en}} On March 3, 2021, McConnell broke the NBA record for most steals in a half with 9.{{Cite web|url=https://www.si.com/.amp/nba/2021/03/04/tj-mcconnell-pacers-nba-record-steals-in-half-triple-double|title=T.J. McConnell Breaks NBA Record with 9 First-Half Steals vs. Cavs | Sports Illustrated|date=March 3, 2021|access-date=March 4, 2021|archive-date=April 16, 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230416064910/https://www.si.com/.amp/nba/2021/03/04/tj-mcconnell-pacers-nba-record-steals-in-half-triple-double|url-status=dead}} He also became the first player since [[Mookie Blaylock]] in 1998 to record a triple-double with points, steals, and assists, as well as the first one to do so off the bench.{{Cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/news/t-j-mcconnell-sets-nba-record-with-9-steals-in-first-half|title = T.J. McConnell sets NBA record with 9 steals in first half| website=[[NBA.com]] }} In 69 contests (three starts) for Indiana, McConnell averaged 8.6 points, and posted career-highs in rebounds (3.7), assists (6.6), and steals (1.9).{{Cite web|title=T.J. McConnell 2020-21 Stats per Game|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/player/gamelog/_/id/2530530/type/nba/year/2021|access-date=May 4, 2026|website=espn.com|language=en}} On August 2, 2021, the Pacers re-signed McConnell to a four-year, $35 million contract.{{Cite web|url = https://www.indycornrows.com/2021/8/2/22603028/t-j-mcconnell-agrees-to-4-year-35m-deal-to-return-to-pacers|title = T.J. McConnell agrees to 4-year, $35M deal to return to Pacers|date = August 2, 2021|access-date = October 17, 2021|archive-date = April 12, 2023|archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20230412052308/https://www.indycornrows.com/2021/8/2/22603028/t-j-mcconnell-agrees-to-4-year-35m-deal-to-return-to-pacers|url-status = dead}} On December 1, he suffered a right wrist injury in a 111–114 loss to the [[2021–22 Atlanta Hawks season|Atlanta Hawks]]. On December 7, McConnell underwent surgery and was ruled out for at least 10-to-12 weeks.{{Cite web |title=T.J. McConnell Undergoes Successful Surgery on Right Wrist |url=https://www.nba.com/pacers/news/tj-mcconnell-undergoes-successful-surgery-right-wrist |access-date=March 18, 2022 |website=NBA}} Due to his injury, he only appeared in 27 games (starting eight), in which he averaged 8.5 points, 3.3 rebounds, and 4.9 assists.{{Cite web|title=T.J. McConnell 2021-22 Stats per Game|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/player/gamelog/_/id/2530530/type/nba/year/2022|access-date=May 4, 2026|website=espn.com|language=en}} On January 16, 2023, McConnell recorded a career-high 29 points, scoring 25 points in the first half, in a loss to the [[2022–23 Milwaukee Bucks season|Milwaukee Bucks]].{{Cite web |title=Pacers' T.J. McConnell: Pours in career-high 29 points |url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/pacers-t-j-mcconnell-pours-in-career-high-29-points/#:~:text=McConnell%20contributed%20a%20career%2Dhigh,132%2D119%20loss%20to%20Milwaukee. |access-date=January 16, 2023 |website=CBSsports.com| date=January 16, 2023 }} On January 21, as a starter, McConnell recorded his third career triple-double with 18 points, 12 assists, and 10 rebounds.{{Cite web |title=T.J. McConnell nets third career triple-double in Pacers loss to Suns |url=https://www.azdesertswarm.com/procats/2023/1/22/23566139/tj-mconnell-triple-double-pacers-suns-arizona-wildcats-basketball |access-date=January 22, 2023 |website=AZdesertswarm.com|date=January 22, 2023 }} He appeared in 75 games (starting six) for Indiana in the [[2022–23 NBA season|2022–23 season]], averaging 8.7 points, 3.1 rebounds, and 5.3 assists.{{Cite web|title=T.J. McConnell 2022-23 Stats per Game|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/player/gamelog/_/id/2530530/type/nba/year/2023|access-date=May 4, 2026|website=espn.com|language=en}} On May 2, 2024, McConnell recorded a playoff career-high 20 points and nine rebounds in a 120–98 series-clinching victory against the [[2023–24 Milwaukee Bucks season|Milwaukee Bucks]] in Game 6 of the [[2024 NBA playoffs|First Round]].{{Cite news|url=https://abcnews.go.com/Sports/bench-players-obi-toppin-tj-mcconnell-lead-pacers/story?id=109891976|title=Bench players Obi Toppin, T.J. McConnell lead Pacers into semis|publisher=[[ABC News (United States)|ABC News]]|date=May 2, 2024|access-date=May 3, 2024}} He made 71 appearances (including four starts) for Indiana during the [[2023–24 NBA season]], averaging a career-high 10.2 points, 2.7 rebounds, and 5.5 assists.{{Cite web|title=T.J. McConnell 2023-24 Stats per Game|url= https://www.espn.com/nba/player/gamelog/_/id/2530530/type/nba/year/2024|access-date=May 4, 2026|website=espn.com|language=en}} On August 30, 2024, McConnell signed a four-year, $45 million contract extension with the Pacers.{{Cite web |date=August 30, 2024 |title=Report: Pacers sign T.J. McConnell to four-year, $45M extension |url=https://www.sportsnet.ca/nba/article/report-pacers-sign-t-j-mcconnell-to-four-year-45m-extension/ |access-date=September 1, 2024 |website=Sportsnet}} On December 8, McConnell scored a career-high 30 points, going 14-for-19 with one rebound, six assists, two blocks, and two steals in a 113–109 loss to the [[2024–25 Charlotte Hornets season|Charlotte Hornets]].{{Cite web|title=Pacers waste 30 points from T.J. McConnell in gutpunch loss to Hornets|url=https://www.indystar.com/story/sports/nba/pacers/2024/12/08/indiana-pacers-charlotte-hornets-live-score-highlights-stats/76665772007/|access-date=December 24, 2024|website=indystar.com|language=en}} He played in 79 games (including one start) for Indiana during the regular season, posting averages of 9.1 points, 2.4 rebounds, and 4.4 assists.{{Cite web|title=T.J. McConnell 2024-25 Stats per Game|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/player/gamelog/_/id/2530530/type/nba/year/2025|access-date=May 4, 2026|website=espn.com|language=en}} On June 11, 2025, McConnell recorded 10 points, five assists, and five steals in Game 3 of the [[2025 NBA Finals|NBA Finals]] against the [[2024–25 Oklahoma City Thunder season|Oklahoma City Thunder]]. He became the first player to record 10+ points, 5+ assists, and 5+ steals off the bench in an NBA Finals game. On January 16, 2026, McConnell joined [[Lou Williams]] as the only players in NBA history to record 3,000 assists off of the bench.{{Cite web|title=Pacers T.J. McConnell is second player with 3,000 assists off the bench|url=https://sports.yahoo.com/articles/pacers-t-j-mcconnell-second-005737428.html|access-date=March 5, 2026|website=sports.yahoo.com|language=en}} He made 56 appearances (including four starts) for the Pacers during the [[2025–26 NBA season|2025–26 campaign]], recording averages of 9.4 points, 2.2 rebounds, and 5.1 assists.{{Cite web|title=T.J. McConnell 2025-26 Stats per Game|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/player/gamelog/_/id/2530530/type/nba/year/2026|access-date=May 4, 2026|website=espn.com|language=en}} For the season, McConnell led the NBA with a 4.48 assists:turnover ratio (minimum 200 assist).{{cite web|url=https://www.foxsports.com/nba/stats?category=assists&sort=astto&season=2025&seasonType=reg&sortOrder=desc|title=National Basketball Association: Assist Stats|accessdate=June 16, 2026|publisher=[[Fox Sports]]}}{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/stats/help/statminimums|title=NBA Advanced Stats: Statistical Minimums to After many successful runs with the [[Chartiers Valley High School]] boys' and girls' teams, he became the head coach of the [[Bishop Canevin High School]] boys' team, a position vacated by T.J.'s roommate at [[Duquesne University]], Gino Palmosina. Tim Sr. often jogs at Collier Park, the location of the T.J. McConnell Memorial Court.{{cite web|url=http://www.thealmanac.net/article/20150130/SPORTS/150139999|title=McConnell wins 500th game at Chartiers Valley|access-date=November 9, 2017}} He played at [[Waynesburg University|Waynesburg College]] from 1984 to 1986.{{cite news|last1=Smith|first1=Nathan|title=McConnell reaches coaching milestone with Chartiers Valley|url=https://archive.triblive.com/news/mcconnell-reaches-coaching-milestone-with-chartiers-valley/#axzz3pjAL8o1y|access-date=October 22, 2024|newspaper=Pittsburgh Tribune-Review|date=February 4, 2015}}{{cite web|url=http://mobile.philly.com/beta?wss=/philly/sports/sixers&id=364669771|title=Please wait while you are redirected|website=mobile.philly.com|access-date=November 9, 2017}} T.J. has two siblings: Matthew and [[Megan McConnell|Megan]]. Matthew "Matty" McConnell played basketball for [[Robert Morris University]] until graduating in 2019. Matthew and T.J. are the only two players in [[Chartiers Valley High School]] basketball history to accrue 2,000 points in their high school careers. Megan McConnell, also a former star basketball player at Chartiers Valley High School, was a lead guard at Duquesne University and played for the [[Phoenix Mercury]]. T.J.'s aunt, [[Suzie McConnell-Serio]], was an All-American at Penn State (1985–1988), Olympic gold medalist, and [[Women's National Basketball Association|WNBA]] standout who was inducted to the [[Women's Basketball Hall of Fame]] in 2008. She started her college coaching career at Duquesne. T.J. married his high school sweetheart, Valerie, in Bridgeville, Pennsylvania, at Holy Child Parish (now known as Corpus Christi Parish) in 2017. Then-teammate [[Nik Stauskas]], and his Duquesne roommate, Palmosina, served as groomsmen.{{cite web | last=Ellis | first=Josh | title=Sixers' T.J. McConnell gets married as Nik Stauskas plays groomsman | website=NBC Sports Philadelphia | date=2017-09-10 |
